title: Nanavira: consciousness is reflexive presence, not a thing requiring vimarśa
central_reading: Nanavira's account treats consciousness as the presence of a phenomenon, reflexively given. The Trika criticism assumes consciousness is a 'thing' needing an extra property (vimarśa), but for Nanavira reflexivity is structural to presence itself.

claims.text: Consciousness (viññāṇa) is the presence of a phenomenon, and that presence is reflexively given. 'There is eye-consciousness — eye-consciousness is present reflexively.' Consciousness is not an entity or thing that requires an added property (vimarśa) to be sentient. It is the presence-of-phenomena, and presence as such is inherently reflexive. The immediate/reflexive presence distinction shows that reflexivity is built into the structure of experience, not added by a separate principle.
claims.source_span: Notes on Dhamma — Viññāṇa, §d on reflexive presence
claims.hetu: consciousness is presence of phenomena, not an entity; presence is reflexively given
claims.sadhya: reflexivity is structural to Nanavira's account, not an added property
claims.vyapti: If consciousness is presence and presence is reflexively given, then reflexivity is built into the structure of experience.
claims.falsifier: Show that Nanavira's 'reflexive presence' is compatible with a purely structural account that lacks sentience — i.e., that presence could be reflexively given without being experienced.

targets.rationale: Direct account of reflexive presence from primary text.
Shows Trika's framing of the issue may misrepresent the Buddhist position.
